A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GET framework for generalized category discovery. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original GET benchmark results, ablations, NEV experiments, visualizations, and supplementary analyses, including repeated-run statistics.

after.justification: v3 retains original GET experiments and reports additional results on TV-100, medical and soybean datasets, together with new controlled analyses.

M1.justification: The TES mapping, loss components, dual-branch training, CICO, and visual-branch inference are retained. The no-distillation TES variant applied to soybean datasets in v3 was already evaluated in v2 Table 7. Newly explaining anchor averaging and testing alternative configurations do not establish a revised proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: v3 adds TV-100, colorectal histology dataset NCT-CRC-HE, and SoyAgeing-R1/R3/R4 evaluations, substantially extending the represented domains. The soybean experiments also address unavailable base-class names. The original standard benchmarks, NEV, and Clevr-4 texture evaluation remain.

E2.justification: v3 Tables 1–2 add µGCD and LegoGCD to relevant benchmark comparisons. Table 5 adds BLIP and BLIP-2 captioning alongside their retained VQA configurations. Table 21 introduces direct grouping by retrieved WordNet/CC3M names, distinct from v2's retrieval embeddings followed by dual-branch training. Earlier comparators, including PromptCAL-CLIP, remain.

E3.justification: Standard benchmark splits, ACC, batch sizes, and 200-epoch training budgets remain. v3 adds estimated-class-count evaluation and controlled prompt, anchor, and loss-weight settings, and specifies class splits for TV-100 and the medical dataset. It reports λc=1 throughout, replacing v2's ambiguous '2 and 1, respectively'; this revises the stated setting without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds prompt sensitivity tests, classifier-versus-sample-anchor ablation, and λc sensitivity analysis in Tables 6, 19, and 22. Table 17 evaluates downstream GET accuracy using estimated class counts, whereas v2 only reported count estimates. Captioning comparisons and experiments without base-class names further expand the examination of practical assumptions. Existing ablations and visual analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions state that results average three independent runs and provide the same main-result and branch standard deviations. The Clevr-4 texture experiment retains five-run reporting. v3 introduces no new uncertainty-estimation procedure, significance test, or seed-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Main GET accuracies remain unchanged, including 77.0% on CUB and 78.5% on Stanford Cars. v3 adds extensive results, including 57.1% All accuracy on TV-100 and 83.8% on NCT-CRC-HE. Table 17 reports 75.6% on CUB using estimated class counts, an additional setting rather than a v2-to-v3 performance loss. The added LegoGCD comparator ties GET at 62.4% ImageNet-1K All accuracy.

T1.justification: The problem assumptions and substantive mathematical objectives are retained, with equation renumbering, inline presentation, and clarification of contrastive-temperature notation. No theorem, proof, or derivation is added. The omitted ACC equation is the standard formula for the retained metric, rather than a removed theoretical contribution.

C1.justification: The central claims that TES enables use of CLIP's text encoder without sample class names, and that dual-branch/CICO training improves GCD, remain unchanged. v3 shortens the contribution list, but retains the backbone investigation and ImageNet-R claims elsewhere. The abstract's broad performance claim is also retained.

C2.justification: v3 explains captioning failures through emphasis on poses and scenes rather than class identity, discusses applicability without base-class names, and motivates dynamic sample-derived anchors. Its CLIP-overlap discussion now distinguishes methodological, future-data, and practical arguments. These extend existing interpretations; the equal-weighting-of-modalities limitation remains unchanged.

D1.justification: The code statement changes from promised release to reported availability, which cannot be independently verified from the PDFs. v3 adds BLIP model variants and total parameter counts, RandomCrop disclosure, explicit anchor averaging, and clearer regularization settings. Conversely, it omits v2's explicit ACC/Hungarian explanation and V2 protocol designation. Most implementation details and pseudocode are retained in the supplement.

R1.justification: v3 adds TextGCD, LegoGCD, recent vision-language work, and references supporting new datasets and applications. It expands discussion of the already-cited µGCD work and contrasts GET with TextGCD's external lexicon and LLM usage. The Hungarian-algorithm citation is removed. These update the existing research positioning without replacing its overall framing.

P1.justification: v3 substantially reorganizes the narrative: it condenses the introduction and experimental discussion, moves detailed settings, pseudocode, and the backbone investigation into the supplement, and reorganizes supplementary material into multiple dedicated sections. It also adds GET to the title, revises author information, and removes biographies.

P2.justification: The journal-style presentation changes to a conference-style layout, and the formerly single-column appendix becomes predominantly two-column supplementary material. Numerous retained displays are resized or relocated, including the backbone figures. New analysis tables are added, the TES comparison gains parameter and captioning entries, and the NEV results display is expanded to include TV-100.

improvement.justification: v3 improves validation of practical assumptions: Table 17 measures performance with estimated class counts, while new domain evaluations and prompt, anchor, and loss-weight analyses make applicability and design choices better assessable. Clearer implementation reporting also helps. These gains outweigh limited reporting weaknesses, including the retained claim of outperforming every comparator despite the new ImageNet-1K tie with LegoGCD in Table 2. The original method and main benchmark results remain unchanged.
